Rashi on Zevachim 11a:20:1.hebrew: אמרו דבר אחד: that Rabbi Eliezer also disqualifies other offerings slaughtered for the sake of a Pesach offering at its designated time, or for the sake of a ḥatat offering all year round, and Rabbi Yoḥanan derives this from a baraita below.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:16:1.english: Rabbi Yehoshua declares it fit - because he considers the Paschal offering to be like other sacrifices for the rest of the year.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:16:2.english: Ben Beteira invalidates it - the Gemara will explain their reasoning.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:18:1.hebrew: מכשיר היה בן בתירא בפסח ששחטו שחרית לשמו - דפסח בשאר ימות השנה חשיב ליה.:אבדעקמוןרו
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:18:1.english: Ben Beteira would deem fit a Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning [of Passover eve] for its sake - for he considers it a Paschal offering from the rest of the days of the year.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:18:2.hebrew: בן בתירא פוסל - בגמרא מפרש להו.:אבדעקמוןרו
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:18:2.english: Ben Beteira deems it unfit - The Gemara explains his reasoning.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:5:1.english: And they shall not profane the holy things - There is no profanation when they offer them for the sake of an offering higher than themselves:

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:6:1.english: That are to be set apart - That is, untithed produce, as it is written: "they will set apart" [using] a future tense verb. And it concludes here in Sanhedrin, chapter "These are those who are burned," that the profanation is derived from teruma, as it is written concerning it: "and die in it if they profane it":

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:7:1.english: If so - For according to Rabbi Shimon, brother of Azarya, it came only to write: "and they shall not profane that which was set apart" [in the past tense]. What is written [using] a future tense verb "which they will set apart" means that this [other derivation] is also to be derived from it:

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:8:1.hebrew: בעי רבי זירא - לשום גבוה מהן כשרים דקתני: כשרין ואין מרצין קאמר כתנא קמא, ולא פליג אלא בנמוך, דקאמר: פסולים לגמרי.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:8:2.hebrew: ובתרתי פליגי - לשם גבוה מכשיר לגמרי, ובנמוך פסיל לגמרי; ואילו רבנן בתרוייהו מכשירים ואין מרצין קאמרי.

Steinsaltz In-Depth comment #1 on Zevach.english: According to the first _tanna_, any offering that is sacrificed for the sake of another type of offering is fit but does not fulfill its owner’s obligation. Shimon, brother of Azarya, maintains, according to this suggestion, that an offering that is sacrificed for the sake of an offering of greater sanctity than it is fit and fulfills its owner's obligation, whereas an offering that is sacrificed for the sake of an offering of lesser sanctity than it is disqualified (Rashi). It might seem that he could have asked in another way: Perhaps Shimon, brother of Azarya, does not disagree about offerings sacrificed for the sake of less sacred ones, and when he said they are unfit, he only meant that they do not fulfill the owner's obligation, as we found this phrasing used elsewhere. However, it can be said that from the phrase “and they shall not profane,” which is the source for Rabbi Shimon ben Azarya’s statement (see above), it is clear that there is indeed profanation when one sacrifices for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity (Shita Mekubbetzet, and similarly in Tosafot above on 4b).

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 11b:8.english: ב Rabbi Zeira asks: Is the intention of Shimon, brother of Azarya, that if one slaughtered them for the sake of offerings of greater sanctity than theirs, they are fit but do not fulfill the owner's obligation to God, as is the opinion of the Rabbis in the mishna? And if so, when Shimon, brother of Azarya, disagrees with the Rabbis, he disagrees about only one matter, namely, regarding those offerings slaughtered for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity, which in his opinion are completely unfit. Or perhaps his intention is that offerings slaughtered for the sake of offerings of greater sanctity are both fit and fulfill the owner's obligation, and according to this, he disagrees about two matters. For in the opinion of the Rabbis, if one slaughtered them for the sake of offerings of greater sanctity, they are fit, but they do not fulfill the owner's obligation.

Zevachim 11a:20.english: The mishna teaches: Yosef ben Ḥoni says: Other offerings that are slaughtered for the sake of a Pesach offering or a ḥatat offering are unfit. Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Yosef ben Ḥoni and Rabbi Eliezer said the same thing, i.e., Rabbi Eliezer agrees with Yosef ben Ḥoni.

Zevachim 11b:16.english: MISHNA: With regard to the Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan, the day when the Paschal offering should be slaughtered in the afternoon, if he did so not for its sake, Rabbi Yehoshua deems it fit as though it were slaughtered on the thirteenth of Nisan. Ben Beteira deems it unfit as though it were slaughtered in the afternoon of the fourteenth.

Zevachim 11b:18.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Elazar says that Rabbi Oshaya says: Just as ben Beteira disqualifies a Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan not for its sake, so too, ben Beteira would deem fit a Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan for its sake, as he held that the entire day, the fourteenth of Nisan, is its designated time.

Zevachim 11b:8.english: Rabbi Zeira raises a dilemma: According to Shimon, brother of Azarya, who says that less sacred offerings sacrificed for the sake of more sacred offerings are fit, perhaps they are fit but do not fulfill the owner's obligation to God, as the Rabbis hold. If so, when Shimon, brother of Azarya, disagrees with the first _tanna_ in the mishna, he disagrees only with regard to one matter, i.e., that more sacred offerings sacrificed for the sake of less sacred ones are disqualified altogether. Alternatively, perhaps Shimon, brother of Azarya, holds that if less sacred offerings are sacrificed for the sake of more sacred offerings, they are both fit and fulfill the owner's obligation, and he disagrees with the Rabbis about two matters.
